study_identification_part.si4_title: Dynamic gray matter volume changes in pediatric multiple sclerosis: A 3.5 year MRI study

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Assess spatial patterns of gray matter (GM) atrophy in pediatric multiple sclerosis (MS), characterize their longitudinal change (~3.5 years), and evaluate clinical relevance (disability, IQ) using deviations from age- and sex-expected GM trajectories.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: NIH-funded MRI Study of Normal Brain Development; Hospital San Raffaele (HSR)
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly states two groups of healthy controls: (1) 26 sex- and age-matched HC recruited at Hospital San Raffaele (HSR), and (2) 317 pediatric HC from the NIH-funded MRI Study of Normal Brain Development (NIH HC) with longitudinal MRI assessments. The NIH dataset was used to estimate GM developmental trajectories due to difficulty obtaining longitudinal scans from pediatric HC.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: To overcome the difficulty of obtaining longitudinal MRI scans from pediatric HC, 2 groups of pediatric HC were selected for comparison of MRI volumes: (1) a group of 26 sex- and age-matched HC recruited at Hospital San Raffaele (HSR) with no history of neurologic dysfunction and a normal neurologic examination, studied on the same MRI scanner as patients with MS at baseline; and (2) a group of 317 pediatric HC from the NIH-funded MRI Study of Normal Brain Development (NIH HC) with longitudinal MRI assessments for brain volume quantification (median follow-up 3.6 years, range 0.9-5.4 years).

rci2_hc_n.reason: The paper clearly states that the NIH HC dataset consisted of 317 pediatric HC with longitudinal MRI assessments, and the HSR HC group consisted of 26 sex- and age-matched HC. The 317 NIH HC were the primary dataset used for estimating GM developmental trajectories.

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: SPM12; Longitudinal registration; DARTEL (diffeomorphic anatomical registration using exponentiated lie algebra); Segmentation; MNI normalization; 4-mm Gaussian smoothing; Lesion refilling
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The paper provides detailed preprocessing steps: (1) within-subject serial longitudinal registration in SPM12, (2) tissue segmentation, (3) DARTEL registration to create group templates, (4) affine transformation to MNI space, (5) intensity modulation using Jacobian determinants, (6) spatial normalization and smoothing with 4-mm Gaussian kernel. Lesion refilling was also performed before GM volumetric analysis.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: Regional GM growth modeling in HC and the evaluation of deviations from normative data in patients with MS required the alignment of participant images to Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) standard space. Taking into account the longitudinal consistency of MRI scans belonging to the same participant, within-subject serial longitudinal registration as implemented in SPM 12 was used to align the available 3D T1-weighted images (either 2 or 3). [...] Then, GM and WM segmented images of all participants, in the closest possible rigid-body alignment with each other, were used to produce initial GM and WM templates and to drive the deformation to the templates. At each iteration, the deformations, calculated using the diffeomorphic anatomical registration using exponentiated lie algebra (DARTEL) registration method, were applied to GM and WM, with an increasingly good alignment of participant morphology, to produce templates. [...] modulated, and smoothed with a 4-mm Gaussian kernel using the DARTEL tool 'Normalize to MNI space.' [...] The 3D T1-weighted images were coregistered and resliced to match the T2-weighted scans before identification and segmentation of the T1-hypointense lesions and underwent lesion refilling before GM volumetric analysis.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.location: DeMeo2019.pdf.md: Methods / GM volume analysis, L90-L92; Methods / Lesional analysis, L88

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Pediatric MS shows widespread GM deviations from normative trajectories with progression notably in deep GM; deviations associate with greater disability and lesion burden, while higher IQ relates to reduced deviations.
